planting.note: Plant divisions in early spring into moist, well-drained soil in partial shade; Moulin Rouge is a compact selection grown for having some of the darkest, nearly black-red flowers in the genus.

directions: Moulin Rouge bears a dense button-like umbel of deep red florets ringed by a starry collar of pointed, red bracts with purple-black tips, giving an overall near-black effect that is among the darkest of any masterwort cultivar. It is a compact, well-branched selection that blooms from early into late summer. Grow in moist, well-drained soil in partial shade, since the darkest coloring and best vigor develop where summers stay cool; full sun is tolerated only where heat and drought are not extreme. Divide congested clumps every three to four years in early spring to maintain vigor.

planting.note: Plant divisions in early spring into rich, consistently moist soil in partial shade; Abbey Road was introduced in the early 2000s for its deep reddish-purple flowers on dark purple stems.

directions: Abbey Road produces dome-shaped clusters of tiny deep reddish-purple flowers surrounded by an elegant ruff of red-and-cream papery bracts, carried on upright, deep purple stems well above the deeply divided dark green foliage. It blooms for weeks from late spring into early summer, with sporadic repeat flowering through summer in favorable conditions. Grow in rich, medium to consistently moist, well-drained soil in full sun to partial shade, performing best where summers stay cool; hot, humid, or dry conditions are poorly tolerated. Divide congested clumps every three to four years in early spring.

planting.note: Plant divisions in early spring into moist, humus-rich soil in partial shade; Snow Star is grown for its large, pure white papery bracts.

directions: Snow Star carries large, pure white, green-flushed flowers with green-tipped papery bracts on wiry stems held clear of the lobed green foliage, blooming from June through September. Grow in moist but well-drained, humus-rich soil in partial shade, where the clean white coloring holds best and plants stay vigorous through the season. The long-lasting flowers are good for cutting. Divide congested clumps every three to four years in early spring to maintain flowering vigor.

planting.note: Plant divisions in early spring into evenly moist, well-drained soil in sun to partial shade; Lars is a Danish-raised red selection valued for its intense, sustained flower color.

directions: Lars bears tiny flowers gathered into umbels of an intense, sustained red-pink that lightens only slightly as the blooms mature, held above a clump of green foliage through summer. It grows well in anything from full sun to mostly shade provided moisture is regular, and tolerates a wide range of soils from acidic to alkaline. Grow in evenly moist, well-drained soil in partial shade for the best color retention in warmer gardens. Divide congested clumps every three to four years in early spring to maintain vigor.

planting.note: Plant divisions in early spring into moist, fertile soil in full sun to partial shade; this strain was selected from seedlings grown by Lincolnshire gardener Gill Richardson and named in her honor.

directions: Gill Richardson Group is an upright, clump-forming selection bearing umbels of tiny crimson-red flowers surrounded by prominent, dark-tipped red bracts above dark green leaves, with flower stems and young foliage flushed burgundy-purple. It tolerates full sun and partial shade and thrives in a wide range of soils including chalk and clay. Divide congested clumps every three to four years in early spring to maintain vigor; it is noted as a strong pollinator plant for bees.

planting.note: Plant divisions in early spring into moist, well-drained soil in full sun to partial shade; Primadonna produces a branching mass of rich ruby and rose pincushion flowers prized for cutting.

directions: Primadonna bears rich pink-and-red flowers from June to September, with dusky overall tones lit by flashes of richer ruby-rose color across a branching, floriferous clump. Grow in moist, well-drained soil of any type in full sun to partial shade; plants perform best where summer heat is moderated and soil moisture stays consistent. The long-lasting flowers are valued both for garden display and as a commercial cut flower. Divide congested clumps every three to four years in early spring to maintain vigor.

planting.note: Plant rhizomes just below the surface in a sheltered woodland bed with rich, humusy, moisture-retentive soil; this Chinese mayapple does not run or go summer-dormant like the American species.

directions: Galaxy was selected through a Japanese nursery from Chinese stock and produces a single hexagonal, green to silvery-green leaf per stalk marked with an irregular, starfish-like black pattern, one of the most striking foliage displays in the genus. Pendulous red flowers hang beneath the mature leaf in spring. Unlike the running, summer-dormant native mayapple, it forms a slowly expanding clump and stays in leaf through the season. Give it part sun to light shade and rich, consistently moist, well-drained soil, since it lacks heat tolerance and performs best where summers stay cool. All parts except the ripe fruit are toxic if ingested.

planting.note: Set divisions or container plants shallowly in rich, consistently moist woodland soil; Audrey is a probable hybrid mayapple that spreads by stolons once established, unlike most clump-forming Podophyllum.

directions: Audrey forms large, convex, starfish-shaped leaves in a glowing amber-to-madder-red that persist in color through the season, with pendant, dark wine-red flowers appearing on the leaf petiole after the leaves mature. It is a probable hybrid mayapple suited to part shade to high overhead shade in rich soil with consistent summer moisture; feeding lightly each spring supports its vigor. Once established it spreads by stolons as far as moist, humus-rich soil allows, making it more of a slow-spreading groundcover than a static clump, so give it room or a contained bed accordingly.

planting.note: Plant divisions in spring in rich, consistently moist, well-drained woodland soil in shade; Strong Silent Type is a vigorous hybrid between a good form of Podophyllum pleianthum and a robust P. delavayi hybrid.

directions: Strong Silent Type is a vigorous hybrid mayapple with large, olive-green leaves touched in mottled light bronze, especially when young, and well-displayed red flowers held beneath the foliage in spring and summer. Grow in rich, consistently moist, well-drained soil in shade, mulching with leaf litter to mimic its native woodland floor and protect emerging shoots from late frost. Its bold scale and vigor make it a dependable anchor plant for a large shaded woodland border.
